summary.headline: EPL Q1 FY27 revenue grew 25.3% (20% underlying ex pass-through) with EBITDA margin at 18.8%; revenue guidance raised to high teens.
summary.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue growth of 25.3%, or 20% underlying excluding pass-through of higher raw material prices, with EBITDA up 15.2% and margin at 18.8% (19.6% underlying). Reported PAT fell 1.4% while PBT rose 10%, which management attributed to a low base-year effective tax rate and phasing. Working capital rose roughly INR 180 crore in the quarter, mainly inventory, which management linked to raw material price inflation and safety stock. Revenue growth guidance was raised from early double digits to high teens for the next few quarters, with the 20% underlying EBITDA margin target held. Europe margins contracted on operational issues and transitional costs, and the Indovida merger received CCI approval but is still pending final approval.

financial_highlights.change: Management says in line with plan; FY PAT expected to grow double digits
Full-year ETR guided at 20-22% vs 18% in FY26

financial_highlights.value: About INR 180 crore (analyst back-calculation from net debt)
financial_highlights.change: FY26 full-year increase cited as about INR 170 crore

financial_highlights.metric: Personal Care & Beyond share of portfolio

segments.name: Beauty & Cosmetics (B&C)
segments.commentary: Growth exceeded 20% in the quarter. Management cites current global market share of 8%, with a target of up to 16% over the next few years.

segments.name: Oral Care
segments.commentary: Growth crossed 20% (management cites 24%), which it calls exceptional and not repeatable every quarter; it normally expects high single-digit growth in this mature category.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 20.2% but margins contracted on operational challenges and transitional costs. Management targets a recovery to a mid-teens margin in coming quarters; manufacturing remains in Poland and Germany.

segments.name: Americas
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 29.4%, but sequential EBITDA and EBIT fell sharply due to investments in capabilities for Brazil and the US; management says underlying margin is stronger than reported.

segments.name: EAP / Thailand
segments.commentary: EAP grew 34.3%. Thailand operations are ramping up with recent multinational customer wins.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth guidance raised from early double digits to high teens for the next few quarters.
Underlying EBITDA margin held at 20%, to be sustained going forward.
Full-year PAT expected to grow double digits; full-year ETR expected at 20-22%.
Steady-state ETR range 18-22%, depending on country profitability mix.
On a steady-state basis, EBITDA expected to grow faster than revenue.
Management expects to operate in a high inflationary environment for some time; expects to fully recover cost increases (raw materials, freight, currency) via pricing.
capex_capacity: Significant step-up in capex and opex ahead of the growth curve, including a B&C centre of excellence in India and embellishment and decoration investments (some still outsourced).
Europe investments in extruded capacity, printing, and B&C die and tooling capability; customer service and printing centralised in Poland.
Thailand plant set up and ramping up.
Americas investments in Brazil and US capabilities.
Indovida merger: CCI approval received; completion said to be on planned timeline, pending remaining approvals.
demand_pricing: Customer contracts are on a blended cost basis, so currency depreciation, raw material and freight increases are recovered via pricing; management says entire Q1 cost impact was recovered, with some lag from certain customers.
Some old-cost inventory flowed through consumption in the quarter.
Revenue growth includes Middle East pricing impact; volume growth not disclosed as mix effects distort it.
Oral Care gains attributed to service and quality retention during the crisis, with wallet and market share gains across regions.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the roughly INR 180 crore rise in working capital, and did receivables jump?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Deepak Goyal said the rise is mainly inventory, from higher raw material prices and building safety stock, plus capex ahead of the curve. Receivables rose in line with pricing, but ageing and quality are under control.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Europe transitional costs and is manufacturing footprint changing again?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Europe had operational challenges now getting focus and expects resolution in coming quarters. Manufacturing stays in Poland and Germany; it did not quantify the transitional cost adjustment.

qa_highlights.question: Does the upgrade to high-teens growth also lift PBT growth, given FX and depreciation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed high-teens revenue and EBITDA growth for the year, with PBT translating to a similar trajectory; PAT was held back by ETR and phasing, with a double-digit FY PAT still expected.

qa_highlights.question: Was there an inventory gain from sharp price moves?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said old inventory did affect consumption costs, but the company recovered the entire cost impact in Q1 and expects to continue doing so.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Americas EBITDA and EBIT fall sequentially?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said revenue includes pass-through pricing, which distorts sequential comparisons, and that investments in Brazil and the US capabilities weigh on margins; underlying margin is higher than reported.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ETR outlook and post-merger tax impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Full-year ETR guided at 20-22% (Q1 22%). Management declined to comment on consolidated post-merger ETR but said Indovida's PAT is in line with EPL's and the deal is EPS accretive.

risks_watch: Europe margin recovery: management says operational issues are being addressed, but timing is not quantified; target is mid-teens margin.
Working capital and net debt rising on inventory build and capex; watch receivables ageing and inventory levels next quarter.
Oral Care growth of 24% described as exceptional and unlikely to repeat; normal mid-to-high single digits expected.
Indovida merger still awaiting final approvals; management cannot share underlying information until then.
Americas margin pressure from ahead-of-curve investments in Brazil and US.
Effective tax rate variability (18-22% range) can keep PAT growth lagging PBT growth.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on top-line momentum and cost recovery, but defensive on margins and PAT, attributing weak Q1 PAT and Americas EBITDA to tax phasing, pricing lag and investment timing. Evasive on Indovida financials and post-merger tax until approvals are complete.
key_quotes: We were able to pass on the entire cost increase through judicious pricing across all our regions and customers.
While Q1 PAT declined by 1.4%, our PBT increased by 10%. The difference is because we are lapping a very low base year ETR, and this will get corrected on full year basis.
So all our customer contracts, Sanjesh, are on blended cost basis. So currency depreciation also gets recovered.
The 24% growth will not be something which we'll be able to deliver every quarter, but this quarter has been exceptional on Oral.
Their PAT is actually in line with the EPL's PAT and hence it's a very, very EPS accretive merger.
We've raised our guidance to high teens for the next few quarters, reflecting our confidence in the underlying momentum of the business.

growth.why: Management raised revenue growth guidance to high teens (midpoint ~17.5%) for the next few quarters, backed by Q1 reported growth of 25.3% (20% underlying), and capex was stepped up ahead of the growth curve across India, Europe, Americas and Thailand, though most projects lack stated sizes or timelines.
